---
title: Wind speed quantile mapping (QM)
---

**Problem.** For several months the DTN wind speed of stations 89002 and 86338 is squashed (smaller and smoother values) while the wind farms keep generating normally. A model fed with this weather would think the wind was weak.

**Fix.** Quantile mapping (QM) per station. Inside the corrupted window, each half-hour keeps its *rank* (is it windy or calm compared with the other half-hours of the same month and time of day?) but takes the *value* that this rank has in the clean years FY23-25.

**Flow**

| Step | Question | Section |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Load the data and the helper functions | 1 |
| 2 | Which days are corrupted, and is the damage something QM can fix? | 2 |
| 3 | Apply QM to the corrupted window | 3 |
| 4 | Test: does QM recover the truth when we corrupt clean data ourselves? | 4 |
| 5 | Save the corrected weather file and show the result | 5 |

**Output:** `data/processed/QM_HistoricWeather_30min.csv`.

## 1. Set-up

```{python}
# =============================================================================
# CELL 1.1 -- Imports, configuration, data and the half-hourly table hh
# apply_qm=False: this file needs the RAW DTN wind speed, because it creates the QM file.
# hh: one row per half-hour with the generation of each wind farm (gen_*), the fleet total (gen_wind) and the
#     wind speed of each station in m/s (ws_<station>); section 3 adds the corrected ws_<station>_qm.
# =============================================================================

import os, sys, warnings

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.dates as mdates
from IPython.display import display
from scipy.stats import rankdata, ks_2samp

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# Find the project root (the folder that contains 'functions/'),
# whether the cwd is the root (VS Code / Jupyter) or analysis/ (quarto render)
ROOT = next(
    p
    for p in [os.getcwd(), os.path.dirname(os.getcwd())]
    if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(p, "functions"))
)
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(ROOT, "functions"))

from utilsConfig import DATA_DIR, make_cfg
from utilsPlot import GREY, ORANGE, PURPLE, add_titles, bottom_legend, table_title
from utilsData import load_generation_inputs, load_weather_history

cfg = make_cfg()
gen_scaled, _, vret_capacity = load_generation_inputs(cfg, DATA_DIR)
weather_hh, weather_raw = load_weather_history(cfg, DATA_DIR, apply_qm=False)

hh = gen_scaled[cfg['wind_assets']].copy()
hh.columns = [f'gen_{a}' for a in cfg['wind_assets']]
for stn in cfg['station_ids']:
    hh[f'ws_{stn}'] = weather_hh[f'wind_speed_ms_{stn}']
hh['gen_wind'] = hh[[f'gen_{a}' for a in cfg['wind_assets']]].sum(axis=1, min_count=1)

idx = hh.index
gen_wind = hh['gen_wind']
QM_STATIONS = [89002, 86338]                 # the two DTN wind stations used by the wind model
WINTER = [10, 11, 12, 1, 2, 3]               # Oct-Mar
REF_END = '2025-07-01'                       # clean reference = FY23-25 (before FY26)
print(f'hh: {hh.shape}, {idx.min()} -> {idx.max()}')
```

The helper functions. `qmap` is the whole idea of QM in a few lines; `apply_qm` runs it group by group. `daily_ratio` and `find_window` detect the corrupted days (section 2). `simulate_qm_recovery` is the test of section 4.

```{python}
# =============================================================================
# CELL 1.2 -- Helper functions
#   daily_ratio           daily mean wind speed / mean daily wind speed of the same month in FY23-25
#   find_window           first and last corrupted day from the daily ratios (rule in section 2)
#   diag                  sd of the wind speed and its Spearman correlation with generation
#   qmap, apply_qm        quantile mapping, group by group (calendar month x half-hour slot)
#   real_sd_ratios        measured squashing (sd corrupted / sd reference) per month
#   simulate_qm_recovery  corrupt clean winters ourselves and measure how much QM recovers
# =============================================================================

def daily_ratio(ws, year, month):
    """Daily mean of `ws` in (year, month) divided by the mean daily mean of the same month in FY23-25."""
    ref = ws[(ws.index < REF_END) & (ws.index.month == month)].resample('D').mean().mean()
    cur = ws[(ws.index.year == year) & (ws.index.month == month)]
    return cur.resample('D').mean() / ref


def find_window(start_ratio, end_ratio, threshold=0.5, run=7):
    """First corrupted day of `start_ratio` and last corrupted day of `end_ratio`.

    A day is flagged when its ratio is below `threshold`. A calm but clean day can also be flagged, so the start
    is the first flagged day whose next `run` days have a median ratio below `threshold`, and the end is the last
    flagged day whose previous `run` days do.
    """
    fwd = start_ratio[::-1].rolling(run, min_periods=run).median()[::-1]       # median of the day and the next run-1
    bwd = end_ratio.rolling(run, min_periods=run).median()                      # median of the day and the previous run-1
    start = start_ratio.index[(start_ratio < threshold) & (fwd < threshold)][0]
    end = end_ratio.index[(end_ratio < threshold) & (bwd < threshold)][-1]
    return start, end


def diag(ws, gen, mask):
    """sd of the wind speed and its Spearman correlation with generation over `mask`."""
    d = pd.DataFrame({'ws': ws[mask], 'gen': gen[mask]}).dropna()
    return {'sd': float(round(d['ws'].std(), 2)), 'spearman': float(round(d['ws'].corr(d['gen'], method='spearman'), 3))}


def qmap(bad_vals, ref_vals):
    """Map corrupted values onto the reference distribution, preserving rank order."""
    # Quantile level of each corrupted value within its own group (rank-based plotting position)
    q = (rankdata(bad_vals) - 0.5) / len(bad_vals)
    # Same quantile levels read off the clean reference distribution
    return np.quantile(ref_vals.dropna(), q)


def apply_qm(ws_bad, ws_all, ref_mask, min_bad=20, min_ref=50):
    """Quantile-map `ws_bad` group by group (calendar month x half-hour slot of the day).

    Args:
        ws_bad: Corrupted values to correct (Series, a subset of ws_all).
        ws_all: Full wind speed series; the reference values are taken from it.
        ref_mask: Boolean array over ws_all.index marking the clean reference half-hours.
        min_bad, min_ref: Minimum group sizes; smaller groups are left unchanged.

    Returns:
        (corrected Series on ws_bad.index, number of half-hours mapped,
         skipped groups as (month, slot, n_bad, n_ref)).
    """
    idx_all = ws_all.index
    slot_all = idx_all.hour * 2 + idx_all.minute // 30
    slot_bad = ws_bad.index.hour * 2 + ws_bad.index.minute // 30
    out = ws_bad.copy()
    n_mapped, skipped = 0, []
    for (m, s), g in ws_bad.groupby([ws_bad.index.month, slot_bad]):
        ref_vals = ws_all[ref_mask & (idx_all.month == m) & (slot_all == s)]
        # Skip groups too small to estimate quantiles
        if len(g) >= min_bad and len(ref_vals.dropna()) >= min_ref:
            out.loc[g.index] = qmap(g.values, ref_vals)
            n_mapped += len(g)
        else:
            skipped.append((m, s, len(g), len(ref_vals.dropna())))
    return out, n_mapped, skipped


def real_sd_ratios(ws, bad, ref):
    """sd(corrupted) / sd(reference) for each month of the Oct-Mar season (0.3 if undefined)."""
    idx = ws.index
    ratios = {}
    for m in WINTER:
        b = ws[bad & (idx.month == m)].dropna()
        r = ws[ref & (idx.month == m)].dropna()
        ratios[m] = b.std() / r.std() if r.std() > 0 else 0.3
    return ratios


def simulate_qm_recovery(ws, sd_ratios, windows, ref_all):
    """Corrupt clean winters ourselves, run QM and measure how close it gets to the truth.

    For each (label, start, end) window: squeeze the values towards the monthly median by
    `sd_ratios`, smooth with a 3-point moving average, apply QM with the other clean winters
    as reference (the simulated one is excluded), then compare with the original (true) values.

    Returns:
        DataFrame with one row per (window, month): mean and sd of the truth / squashed / QM series,
        the KS distance to the truth (0 = identical distribution) and the errors of the monthly mean and sd.
    """
    idx = ws.index
    rows = []
    for sim_label, sim_start, sim_end in windows:
        sim_mask = (idx >= sim_start) & (idx < sim_end)

        # Fake corruption
        ws_fake = ws[sim_mask].copy()
        for m in WINTER:
            m_mask = ws_fake.index.month == m
            if m_mask.sum() == 0:
                continue
            vals = ws_fake[m_mask]
            med = vals.median()
            # Keep the median, scale the deviation by the sd ratio
            ws_fake.loc[m_mask] = med + (vals - med) * sd_ratios[m]
        ws_fake = ws_fake.rolling(3, center=True, min_periods=1).mean().clip(lower=0)

        # QM with the simulated winter excluded from the reference
        ws_recovered, _, _ = apply_qm(ws_fake, ws, ref_all & ~sim_mask)

        for m_per in sorted(set(idx[sim_mask].to_period('M'))):
            mm = sim_mask & (idx >= m_per.start_time) & (idx <= m_per.end_time)
            d = pd.DataFrame({'true': ws[mm], 'squashed': ws_fake.reindex(idx[mm]),
                              'qm': ws_recovered.reindex(idx[mm])}).dropna()
            rows.append({'sim': sim_label, 'month': m_per.strftime('%Y-%m'),
                         'mean_true': d['true'].mean(), 'mean_squashed': d['squashed'].mean(), 'mean_qm': d['qm'].mean(),
                         'sd_true': d['true'].std(), 'sd_squashed': d['squashed'].std(), 'sd_qm': d['qm'].std(),
                         'ks_squashed': ks_2samp(d['squashed'], d['true']).statistic,
                         'ks_qm': ks_2samp(d['qm'], d['true']).statistic})
    out_df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    for key in ['mean', 'sd']:
        for kind in ['squashed', 'qm']:
            out_df[f'{key}_err_{kind}'] = (out_df[f'{key}_{kind}'] - out_df[f'{key}_true']).abs()
    return out_df
```

## 2. Detect the corrupted window

**Rule.** For each day, the ratio of its mean wind speed to the mean daily wind speed of the same month in FY23-25. Clean days sit around 1 (a calm day rarely goes below 0.5), corrupted days around 0.2-0.5. A day is flagged when the ratio is below 0.5. A single calm day can be flagged too, so the window starts at the first flagged day followed by a week of mostly flagged days, and ends at the last flagged day preceded by one. October 2025 is searched for the start and April 2026 for the end (the months where the monthly wind speed leaves its usual range, Fig 2.2).

The detected window must equal `cfg['corruption_window']` in `utilsConfig.py`, which the other notebooks use (the cell stops otherwise).

```{python}
# =============================================================================
# CELL 2.1 -- First and last corrupted day of each station (find_window) and Fig 2.1
# =============================================================================

THRESHOLD = 0.5
ratios, rows = {}, []
for stn in QM_STATIONS:
    ws = hh[f'ws_{stn}']
    ratios[stn] = (daily_ratio(ws, 2025, 10), daily_ratio(ws, 2026, 4))
    start, end = find_window(*ratios[stn], threshold=THRESHOLD)
    rows.append({'station': stn, 'first corrupted day': start.date(), 'last corrupted day': end.date(),
                 'days': (end - start).days + 1})
window_tbl = pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index('station')
table_title('Table 2.1 - Corrupted window found in the data', f'daily mean / same-month mean of FY23-25 below {THRESHOLD}')
display(window_tbl)

CORRUPT_START = pd.Timestamp(window_tbl['first corrupted day'].min())
CORRUPT_END = pd.Timestamp(window_tbl['last corrupted day'].max()) + pd.Timedelta(hours=23, minutes=30)
assert (str(CORRUPT_START.date()), str(CORRUPT_END.date())) == tuple(cfg['corruption_window']), \
    f"detected window {CORRUPT_START.date()} - {CORRUPT_END.date()} differs from cfg['corruption_window']"

# Masks used in the rest of the file
bad_full = (idx >= CORRUPT_START) & (idx <= CORRUPT_END)            # the whole corrupted window
ref_oct_apr = (idx < REF_END) & idx.month.isin(WINTER + [4])        # clean Oct-Apr months: the QM reference
bad = bad_full & idx.month.isin(WINTER)                             # Oct-Mar part of the window (test of section 4)
ref = (idx < REF_END) & idx.month.isin(WINTER)                      # clean Oct-Mar months

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 4), sharey=True)
for ax, k, title in [(axes[0], 0, 'October 2025: start'), (axes[1], 1, 'April 2026: end')]:
    for stn, colour in zip(QM_STATIONS, [PURPLE, ORANGE]):
        r = ratios[stn][k]
        ax.plot(r.index.day, r.values, 'o-', color=colour, ms=3, lw=1.2, label=f'Station {stn}')
    edge = CORRUPT_START if k == 0 else CORRUPT_END
    ax.axhline(THRESHOLD, color=GREY, ls='--', lw=1, label=f'Threshold {THRESHOLD}')
    ax.axhline(1, color=GREY, lw=0.6)
    ax.axvline(edge.day, color='black', lw=1, ls=':', label='Detected start / end')
    ax.set(title=title, xlabel='Day of the month')
axes[0].set_ylabel('Daily mean / same-month mean of FY23-25')
fig.tight_layout()
bottom_legend(fig, ncol=4)
add_titles(fig, 'Fig 2.1 - Daily wind speed ratio at the start and the end of the corruption',
           f'Corrupted from {CORRUPT_START:%d %b %Y} to {CORRUPT_END:%d %b %Y} at both stations')
plt.show()
```

**Is it the sensor or the weather?** In Fig 2.2 the monthly wind speed leaves its usual range inside the window (grey) while the wind fleet keeps its usual capacity factor: the farms produced as usual, so the sensor is wrong, not the weather.

```{python}
# =============================================================================
# CELL 2.2 -- Monthly wind speed (station 89002) vs its usual range, and the wind fleet capacity factor
# =============================================================================

ws_monthly = hh['ws_89002'].resample('ME').mean()
ref_months = ws_monthly[ws_monthly.index < REF_END]
band = ref_months.groupby(ref_months.index.month).agg(['min', 'max'])

# Wind fleet capacity factor (generation / capacity of the farms running in each half-hour)
cap_wind_active_hh = sum(vret_capacity[a] * hh[f'gen_{a}'].notna().astype(float) for a in cfg['wind_assets'])
cf_wind_monthly = (hh['gen_wind'] / (0.5 * cap_wind_active_hh)).resample('ME').mean()

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 4))
ax.fill_between(ws_monthly.index, band['min'].reindex(ws_monthly.index.month).values,
                band['max'].reindex(ws_monthly.index.month).values, color=PURPLE, alpha=0.15,
                label='Range of the same month in FY23-25')
ax.plot(ws_monthly, '-o', color=PURPLE, ms=3, label='Mean wind speed, station 89002 (m/s)')
ax.axvspan(CORRUPT_START, CORRUPT_END, color=GREY, alpha=0.15, label='Corrupted window')
ax2 = ax.twinx()
ax2.plot(cf_wind_monthly, color=ORANGE, lw=1.6, label='Wind fleet capacity factor')
ax.set_ylabel('Wind speed (m/s)'); ax2.set_ylabel('Capacity factor')
fig.tight_layout()
bottom_legend(fig)
add_titles(fig, 'Fig 2.2 - Monthly mean wind speed (station 89002) vs wind fleet capacity factor',
           'Measured wind drops sharply while generation stays normal: the weather data is wrong, not the weather')
plt.show()
```

**Can QM fix it?** QM rebuilds the *size* of the values from their *order*, so it only works if the order survived. In the window the spread (sd) collapses, but the Spearman correlation with generation (rank-based) stays at its clean level: the order is intact and QM can rebuild the size.

```{python}
#| label: corruption-hist
# =============================================================================
# CELL 2.3 -- Wind speed distribution, clean Oct-Apr months of FY23-25 vs the corrupted window
# sd and Spearman correlation with generation (diag) in each panel.
# =============================================================================

fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(QM_STATIONS), 1, figsize=(7, 3.2))
for ax, stn in zip(axes, QM_STATIONS):
    ws = hh[f'ws_{stn}']
    x_max = np.ceil(ws[ref_oct_apr].quantile(0.999))
    bins = np.linspace(0, x_max, 61)
    ax.hist(ws[ref_oct_apr].dropna(), bins=bins, density=True, color=PURPLE, alpha=0.3, label='Same-season reference')
    ax.hist(ws[bad_full].dropna(), bins=bins, density=True, color=ORANGE, alpha=0.6, label='Corrupted period')
    r, b = diag(ws, gen_wind, ref_oct_apr), diag(ws, gen_wind, bad_full)
    ax.text(0.99, 0.95, f"sd: {r['sd']:.2f} → {b['sd']:.2f} m/s\nSpearman: {r['spearman']:.3f} → {b['spearman']:.3f}",
            transform=ax.transAxes, ha='right', va='top', fontsize=8)
    ax.set_title(f'Station {stn}', fontsize=10)
    ax.set_xlim(0, x_max)
    ax.set_xlabel('Wind speed (m/s)')
    ax.grid(False)
fig.supylabel('Density', fontsize=9)
fig.tight_layout()
bottom_legend(fig, ncol=2)
add_titles(fig, f'Wind speed corruption ({CORRUPT_START.day} {CORRUPT_START:%b %Y} - {CORRUPT_END.day} {CORRUPT_END:%b %Y})')   # .day: %-d does not work on Windows
plt.show()
```

## 3. Apply quantile mapping

For every (calendar month, half-hour slot) group of the corrupted window: rank the corrupted values, turn the ranks into quantiles, and read the same quantiles off the clean reference (same month and slot, FY23-25). Only weather data is used, no generation, so nothing from the target leaks in. April has only 14 corrupted days, so the minimum group sizes are 5 corrupted and 30 reference values.

By construction the corrected values follow the reference distribution (Table 3.1: ratios close to 1); whether they are *right* is tested in section 4.

```{python}
# =============================================================================
# CELL 3.1 -- QM of the whole corrupted window, both stations
# Output: hh['ws_<station>_qm'] (equal to the original values outside the window).
# =============================================================================

rows = []
for stn in QM_STATIONS:
    ws = hh[f'ws_{stn}']
    qm_vals, n_mapped, skipped = apply_qm(ws[bad_full].dropna(), ws, ref_oct_apr, min_bad=5, min_ref=30)
    hh[f'ws_{stn}_qm'] = ws.copy()
    hh.loc[qm_vals.index, f'ws_{stn}_qm'] = qm_vals
    r, b, q = ws[ref_oct_apr].dropna(), ws[bad_full].dropna(), hh.loc[bad_full, f'ws_{stn}_qm'].dropna()
    rows.append({'station': stn, 'HH mapped': f'{n_mapped:,} / {bad_full.sum():,}', 'groups skipped': len(skipped),
                 'mean ratio before': b.mean() / r.mean(), 'mean ratio after': q.mean() / r.mean(),
                 'sd ratio before': b.std() / r.std(), 'sd ratio after': q.std() / r.std()})
table_title('Table 3.1 - QM of the corrupted window', 'ratio to the clean Oct-Apr months of FY23-25 (1 = same)')
display(pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index('station').round(3))
```

## 4. Test: can QM undo a corruption we make ourselves?

A test where the right answer is known.

1. Take two clean winters, FY24 (Oct 23 - Mar 24) and FY25 (Oct 24 - Mar 25), as the truth.
2. Squash them the way the real corruption did (the real sd ratio of each month, plus a 3-point smoothing).
3. Run QM on the squashed data, using the *other* clean winters as the reference.
4. Compare with the truth: error of the monthly mean and sd (m/s), and the KS distance (0 = identical distribution). *Recovery* is the share of the error QM removes (100% = perfect).

In Fig 4.1 each bar is the error of the monthly sd: orange = squashed, purple = after QM. Half-hour errors are not scored: QM restores the *size* of the values, not their exact timing.

```{python}
# =============================================================================
# CELL 4.1 -- Simulation on clean winters: error of the squashed data and of QM against the truth
# =============================================================================

sim_windows = [('FY24 (Oct23-Mar24)', '2023-10-07', '2024-04-01'),
               ('FY25 (Oct24-Mar25)', '2024-10-07', '2025-04-01')]

sim_res = {}
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(15, 8))
for r_i, stn in enumerate(QM_STATIONS):
    ws = hh[f'ws_{stn}']
    sim_res[stn] = df_sim = simulate_qm_recovery(ws, real_sd_ratios(ws, bad, ref), sim_windows, ref)
    for c_i, (sim, d) in enumerate(df_sim.groupby('sim', sort=False)):
        ax = axes[r_i, c_i]
        x = np.arange(len(d))
        ax.bar(x - 0.2, d['sd_err_squashed'], 0.4, color=ORANGE, alpha=0.85, label='Squashed (no QM)')
        ax.bar(x + 0.2, d['sd_err_qm'], 0.4, color=PURPLE, alpha=0.85, label='After QM')
        ax.set_xticks(x); ax.set_xticklabels(d['month'], rotation=45, fontsize=8)
        ax.set_ylabel('|monthly sd - true sd| (m/s)')
        ax.set_title(f'Station {stn}, {sim}\nMean error: squashed = {d["sd_err_squashed"].mean():.2f}, '
                     f'QM = {d["sd_err_qm"].mean():.2f} m/s', fontsize=9)

rows = []
for stn in QM_STATIONS:
    d = sim_res[stn]
    for label, key in [('Monthly mean error (m/s)', 'mean_err'), ('Monthly sd error (m/s)', 'sd_err'),
                       ('KS distance to truth', 'ks')]:
        b, a = d[f'{key}_squashed'].mean(), d[f'{key}_qm'].mean()
        rows.append({'station': stn, 'metric': label, 'Squashed': b, 'After QM': a, 'Recovery (%)': (1 - a / b) * 100})
val_summary = pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index(['station', 'metric'])
rec_sd = val_summary.xs('Monthly sd error (m/s)', level='metric')['Recovery (%)']

fig.tight_layout()
bottom_legend(fig)
add_titles(fig, 'Fig 4.1 - Simulation on clean winters: how close does QM get to the truth?',
           f'QM removes {rec_sd[89002]:.0f}% / {rec_sd[86338]:.0f}% of the monthly sd error (stations 89002 / 86338)')
plt.show()

table_title('Table 4.1 - Simulation summary: error before and after QM',
            'Average over the 12 simulated months; Recovery = share of the error QM removes (100% = perfect)')
display(val_summary.round(3))
```

## 5. Save the corrected file and show the result

Only `wind_speed_kph` of stations 89002 and 86338 changes, and only inside the corrupted window; everything else is the raw DTN data. The column `qm_corrected` is 1 inside the window.

```{python}
# =============================================================================
# CELL 5.1 -- Save data/processed/QM_HistoricWeather_30min.csv (read by the forecast notebooks)
# Columns per station: temp_c, rh, wind_speed_kph (QM inside the window: m/s x 3.6), wind_dir_degrees; plus qm_corrected.
# =============================================================================

df_dtn = (weather_raw.rename(columns={'ts_local': 'datetime'})
          .loc[lambda d: d['station_id'].isin(QM_STATIONS),
               ['station_id', 'datetime', 'temp_c', 'rh', 'wind_speed_kph', 'wind_dir_degrees']]
          .sort_values(['datetime', 'station_id']))
dfs = []
for stn in QM_STATIONS:
    d = df_dtn[df_dtn['station_id'] == stn].set_index('datetime')[['temp_c', 'rh', 'wind_speed_kph', 'wind_dir_degrees']]
    d.columns = [f'{c}_{stn}' for c in d.columns]
    dfs.append(d)
df_wide = dfs[0].join(dfs[1], how='outer').sort_index()

in_window = (df_wide.index >= CORRUPT_START) & (df_wide.index <= CORRUPT_END)
for stn in QM_STATIONS:
    qm_kph = (hh[f'ws_{stn}_qm'] * 3.6).round(2)                 # the QM series is in m/s; the file stores kph
    overlap = df_wide.index[in_window].intersection(qm_kph.index)
    df_wide.loc[overlap, f'wind_speed_kph_{stn}'] = qm_kph.loc[overlap].values
df_wide['qm_corrected'] = in_window.astype(int)

fpath = os.path.join(DATA_DIR, 'processed', 'QM_HistoricWeather_30min.csv')
os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(fpath), exist_ok=True)
df_wide.to_csv(fpath, index=True, index_label='datetime')
print(f'Saved {fpath}: {len(df_wide):,} rows, {in_window.sum():,} half-hours corrected '
      f'({CORRUPT_START.date()} -> {CORRUPT_END.date()})')
```

The corrected series (purple) continues the seasonal pattern of the clean years, while the original data (dashed orange) drops in the corrupted window.

```{python}
#| label: monthly-ws-after-qm
# =============================================================================
# CELL 5.2 -- Monthly mean wind speed: original (only around the corrupted window) vs QM-corrected
# =============================================================================

fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(QM_STATIONS), 1, figsize=(7, 3.2), sharex=True)
near_window = slice(CORRUPT_START - pd.DateOffset(months=2), CORRUPT_END + pd.DateOffset(months=1))
for ax, stn in zip(axes, QM_STATIONS):
    orig_m = hh[f'ws_{stn}'].resample('MS').mean()
    prod_m = hh[f'ws_{stn}_qm'].resample('MS').mean()
    ax.plot(orig_m.loc[near_window], color=ORANGE, lw=1, ls='--', label='Corrupted (original)')
    ax.plot(prod_m, color=PURPLE, lw=1, label='After QM correction')
    ax.set_title(f'Station {stn}', fontsize=10)
    ax.set_ylim(0, None)
    ax.grid(False)
axes[-1].xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.MonthLocator(bymonth=[1, 7]))
axes[-1].xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter('%b %y'))
fig.supylabel('Monthly mean wind speed (m/s)', fontsize=9)
fig.tight_layout()
bottom_legend(fig, ncol=2)
add_titles(fig, 'Monthly average wind speed after QM calibration')
plt.show()
```
